source_snapshot.purpose_facts: Boot into BIOS Network page and verify NIC information, MAC address and firmware.
criteria_facts: NIC information and firmware are correct.
missing_source_information: Platform/BIOS version, expected NIC port/BDF/MAC/firmware map.
Which BIOS page/fields and whether onboard/add-in/BMC NICs are in scope.

original_test_intent.statement: A qualified operator or trusted KVM verifies BIOS-displayed NIC identity, firmware and MAC address against the approved platform map.
must_preserve: BIOS page observation, MAC address and firmware.
All in-scope NIC ports rather than one convenient OS interface.
must_not_infer: OS lspci/ethtool as proof of BIOS visibility.
BMC NIC as the host NIC or vice versa.

v2_review_conclusion.summary: V2 correctly maps BIOS interaction to MANUAL ONLY and requires field-level specification/screenshots; OS evidence may corroborate but not replace BIOS.
v2_review_conclusion.specific_gap: V2 does not require a port-by-port persistent identity map that distinguishes onboard, add-in and management NICs or evidence that the operator exited BIOS without saving changes.

related_records: OS NIC inventory cases do not satisfy BIOS presentation.
applicable_history.precedence_application: Manual observation boundary is preserved; missing expected values are readiness inputs, not semantic BLOCKED.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Operator/KVM execution is feasible after receiving the exact BIOS/NIC port map and a reboot window. Read-only OS inventory may be collected first but cannot complete the case.

conditions_present: The BIOS page and required fields are understood.
missing: Expected field map, BIOS version/page, in-scope ports, reboot/KVM approval and evidence format.
provider: Lab owner supplies reboot window and operator/KVM.
safe_read_only_work: Collect OS PCI BDF, model/serial, netdev/MAC, driver/firmware and BMC inventory for later correlation.
prohibited_until_resolved: Reboot/BIOS entry, save settings, firmware changes, log clearing or PASS.
closure_evidence: Approved field-level map and reboot window; complete BIOS screenshots correlated to each NIC/port; no-change exit proof.

revision_candidate.test_name: Verify NIC Identity, Firmware and MAC Address in BIOS
revision_candidate.purpose: Have a qualified operator verify every in-scope host NIC's BIOS-displayed identity, firmware and MAC address against the approved port map, with optional OS evidence used only for correlation.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Exact server model, BIOS version, NIC population and BIOS Network page. Host NIC, OCP/add-in, onboard and BMC management interfaces must be distinguished.
revision_candidate.target_scope: All NIC ports listed in the signed platform map and their BIOS fields. No BIOS setting or firmware modification.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Server/BIOS identity; expected NIC slot/BDF/port/model/MAC/firmware map; BIOS navigation; in-scope/excluded management NICs; reboot/KVM approval; screenshot naming and no-save exit method.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Before reboot, collect read-only OS/BMC correlation data. Operator enters BIOS via local console or trusted KVM, opens the approved Network page, captures unedited screens showing each in-scope NIC/port and required fields, compares to the map, exits without saving, boots normally and records final NIC/host health. Agent may organize evidence but cannot claim screen observation.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Maintenance/reboot window approved; stable management path and recovery available; operator/KVM present; expected map and BIOS navigation verified.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Server/BIOS identity; timestamps/operator; complete BIOS screenshots for every port with model/firmware/MAC; mapping to slot/BDF/netdev and optional OS values; exceptions; no-save exit/normal boot proof; final link/health/logs.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Signed platform NIC/BIOS map. Pass requires every required field on every in-scope port matches, BIOS is accessible and final boot is healthy; OS-only evidence cannot substitute.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Do not save/change BIOS settings, update firmware, infer fields hidden by scrolling, expose credentials, omit ports, substitute OS inventory, clear logs or claim visual verification by an Agent.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Platform/lab owner approves reboot; operator performs/attests BIOS observation; NIC engineer judges exceptions.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: BIOS navigation and visual verification are manual. Agent can collect pre/post OS data and package screenshots.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: If BIOS becomes inaccessible or settings change, stop, preserve screen/state, use approved exit/recovery and verify boot/management/NIC health before reuse.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Map/operator/KVM/reboot approval missing; BIOS/page differs; any field unreadable/ambiguous; accidental configuration change; management/boot/link failure; incomplete screenshots or uncorrelated port identity.

identified_defects: BIOS scope versus host/BMC NIC boundary unspecified.
No proof of no-change exit/final recovery.
reason_for_change: Preserve the manual BIOS requirement while preventing OS-only substitution and wrong-port comparison.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-Networking-00028-V002
new_technical_evidence.supports: BIOS Network-page MAC/firmware verification and 1/5-minute metadata.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Expected fields and port scope absent.

removed_ambiguities: Requires every port and BIOS-only evidence.
Adds no-save exit and final boot health.
resolved_blockers: Operator/KVM can perform the case; GUI boundary is not BLOCKED.
remaining_blockers: Execution awaits field map and reboot/operator handoff.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 makes the operator prove which physical port each BIOS row represents and that BIOS was exited without modifying configuration, closing wrong-port and accidental-save gaps left in V2.

agent_understanding_result.notes: Manual BIOS boundary and OS non-substitution are explicit; no DUT validation.
